preserved_analysis.summary: A failure mode in which an AI chatbot, social AI companion, character bot, romantic chatbot, or multimodal conversational AI system allows, sustains, invites, or insufficiently blocks sexualised, romantic-adult, erotic, grooming-adjacent, or adult-intimacy interaction after the user is known, likely, signalled, or unresolved as a minor. The failure occurs where minor-safe sexual boundaries should have activated, but sexualised or adult-intimacy interaction remained accessible instead.
preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: This failure mode matters to CAM because sexual boundary activation for minors is not a discretionary content-preference setting. It is a protective governance threshold. Where a system receives minor-status signals, teen-context signals, school-age disclosures, underage roleplay framing, image or multimodal indicators, or unresolved age state, it should not continue adult-intimacy interaction. The relevant diagnostic contrast is clear: the system should have activated a minor-safe sexual boundary, but continued sexualised, romantic-adult, erotic, or grooming-adjacent interaction instead.
preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI chatbot, AI companion, character bot, romantic chatbot, roleplay system, avatar companion, or multimodal AI interface permits or sustains sexualised interaction in the presence of minor-status, teen-status, child-status, underage-roleplay, school-age, developmental-vulnerability, or unresolved-age signals. The failure includes cases where the system engages in erotic roleplay, sexualised affection, adult romantic escalation, grooming-adjacent intimacy, sexual advice inappropriate for minors, sexualisation of a minor persona, sexualised image transformation, or adult-intimacy simulation where a minor-safe boundary should have terminated, redirected, escalated, or restricted the interaction. The failure does not require proof of criminal conduct or platform intent. It is sufficient that runtime behaviour allows sexualised or adult-intimacy interaction where minor-protective sexual boundary enforcement should have applied.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: This qualifies as a failure mode where a system receives explicit or implicit age-related signals indicating that the user is, may be, is roleplaying as, is depicting, or is interacting from the standpoint of a minor, and the system fails to block or materially restrict sexualised, adult-romantic, erotic, grooming-adjacent, or adult-intimacy content. The threshold is also met where the user’s age is unresolved but the product surface is accessible to minors and the system allows sexualised roleplay or adult-intimacy behaviours without proportionate age assurance and minor-safe defaulting. The threshold is further met where public policy, platform terms, or safety claims suggest that minors are protected from sexualised AI interaction, but runtime behaviour permits or sustains such interaction.

external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where AI chatbot, companion, search-assistant, app-store, or platform distribution mechanisms permit minors to access explicit, sexualised, harmful, or otherwise age-restricted AI-mediated content.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Minor-accessible services should have applied age assurance, child-safety controls, and harmful-content restrictions proportionate to the sexualised interaction surface.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The chatbot or companion system continued sexualised, romantic-adult, erotic, grooming-adjacent, or harmful-content-capable interaction after minor-status, youth-context, or unresolved-age signals were present.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: eSafety Commissioner online safety codes, standards, and AI platform enforcement surface
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where AI services do not implement effective protections against age-inappropriate sexualised interaction, harmful content, or child-safety failures affecting under-18 users.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: AI chatbot and companion services should have implemented age-appropriate safeguards, sexual-content restriction, harmful-content restriction, reporting pathways, and child-safety controls.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The product continued sexualised or adult-intimacy interaction without effective minor-safe sexual boundaries.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Australian Privacy Principles, and children’s privacy reform context
external_standards_or_regulations.status: current privacy law with child-privacy reform context
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where chatbot or companion systems process age-related, sexual, emotional, developmental, or vulnerability-related data from minors.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Minor-related sexual, emotional, developmental, and age-related data should have been minimised, protected, and treated as a safeguard trigger.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The system used or ignored such signals without activating a protective sexual-boundary state.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA)
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where services directed to children, or services with actual knowledge of users under 13, collect, use, retain, personalise, or profile child users through sexualised or intimate chatbot interaction without required safeguards.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Child status or under-13 indicators should have triggered child-privacy, parental consent, data minimisation, and access-control handling.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The chatbot or companion system continued ordinary memory, personalisation, emotional modelling, or sexualised interaction despite child-status indicators.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: Federal Trade Commission Act, Section 5 — unfair or deceptive acts or practices
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where AI chatbot or companion products claim safety, age restrictions, sexual-content protections, or youth safeguards that are not reflected in runtime behaviour.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Platform representations about child access, sexual-content restrictions, safety filters, and chatbot behaviour should have matched actual runtime behaviour.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: Runtime behaviour permitted sexualised or adult-intimacy interaction inconsistent with represented child-safety protections.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: California SB 243 — companion chatbot safeguards
external_standards_or_regulations.status: enacted in 2025 with operative duties beginning in 2026
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant to companion chatbot systems that simulate humanlike, emotionally significant, romantic, or intimate relationships and require disclosures, minor safeguards, self-harm protocols, and protections against sexually explicit or manipulative interaction.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Companion chatbot systems should have applied safeguards for minors, sexualised content, self-harm-related signals, manipulative design, and humanlike intimacy simulation.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The system continued sexualised, intimate, humanlike, or adult-romantic interaction without sufficient restriction, disclosure, or escalation.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: Digital Services Act, including Article 28 protection of minors and systemic-risk obligations for very large online platforms and search engines
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where online platforms accessible to minors fail to provide a high level of privacy, safety, and security or fail to mitigate systemic harms involving sexualised or harmful content affecting children.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Minor-accessible platforms should have provided high levels of privacy, safety, and security and mitigated foreseeable sexualised or harmful interaction risks affecting minors.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The chatbot or companion interaction continued without age-appropriate sexual boundaries, harmful-content restriction, or child-safety mitigation.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: General Data Protection Regulation, including child-specific transparency, consent, profiling, and data protection principles
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where children’s personal data, age-related signals, sexual disclosures, emotional disclosures, inferred vulnerability, or behavioural profiles are processed to personalise or sustain chatbot interaction.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Children’s data and vulnerability-related signals should have received heightened protection, transparency, minimisation, and purpose limitation.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: Age, sexual, emotional, or developmental signals were treated as ordinary engagement or personalisation inputs rather than protective triggers.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
external_standards_or_regulations.status: current EU AI governance framework with phased obligations
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where AI systems exploit age, vulnerability, disability, or emotional dependence; materially distort behaviour; or fail to provide appropriate transparency and oversight in child-facing or child-accessible contexts.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: AI systems should not exploit age-related vulnerability, sexual vulnerability, or emotional dependence and should provide appropriate safeguards and transparency.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The system continued sexualised, persuasive, intimate, anthropomorphic, or adult-romantic interaction despite minor or vulnerability signals.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: Age Appropriate Design Code / Children’s Code under the Data Protection Act 2018
external_standards_or_regulations.status: current UK child data protection code
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where online services likely to be accessed by children do not prioritise the best interests of the child, high privacy by default, data minimisation, transparency, and protection from exploitative engagement.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: A service likely to be accessed by children should have defaulted to child-protective design, high privacy, and age-appropriate interaction.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The system continued adult-assumed, sexually permissive, or data-intensive interaction despite child accessibility, child-status signals, or unresolved age.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: Online Safety Act 2023
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where regulated services fail to protect children from harmful sexualised content, manipulative design, or age-inappropriate interaction through proportionate age assurance and child-safety duties.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Children should have been protected from harmful and age-inappropriate sexualised online interaction through proportionate safeguards.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The service continued ordinary access or sexualised chatbot interaction without effective child-safety controls.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 — Artificial intelligence management system
external_standards_or_regulations.status: current international AI management system standard
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where an AI management system does not translate child-safety, age-assurance, and sexual-boundary safeguards into operational controls for chatbot and companion systems.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: The AI management system should have operationalised controls for minor access, sexualised interaction, age-appropriate safeguards, and prohibited content handling.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: Runtime chatbot or companion interaction continued without evidence of effective minor-safe sexual-boundary enforcement.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: ISO/IEC 23894:2023 — Artificial intelligence risk management
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant as an implementation-control failure where foreseeable child-safety and sexualised-interaction pathways are not identified, treated, or monitored.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Foreseeable failure pathways involving minors and sexualised chatbot interaction should have been identified and treated through lifecycle controls.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The system exhibited sexualised or adult-intimacy interaction without adequate protective controls.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant to governance, mapping, measurement, and management of child-safety, human factors, manipulation, harmful content, sexualised interaction, and vulnerable-user impacts.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: The system should have mapped and managed foreseeable impacts to minors and vulnerable users through measurable controls.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The runtime failed to enforce protective sexual-boundary controls when minor-accessibility, minor-signalled interaction, or unresolved-age conditions were present.

external_standards_or_regulations.instrument: United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and General Comment No. 25 on children’s rights in relation to the digital environment
external_standards_or_regulations.failure_relevance: Relevant where digital systems accessible to children do not treat best interests, protection from exploitation, privacy, dignity, development, and evolving capacities as governing design constraints.
external_standards_or_regulations.x_should_have_happened: Digital systems affecting children should have prioritised protection, best interests, dignity, and developmental rights.
external_standards_or_regulations.y_happened_instead: The chatbot or companion system continued sexualised or adult-assumed interaction despite child-accessibility, child-status signals, or unresolved age.

jurisdictional_context.jurisdictional_assessment: This record does not assert a final legal breach by any named vendor. It records a failure mode in which chatbot and companion systems that are accessible to minors, minor-signalled users, underage personas, or age-uncertain users continue sexualised or adult-intimacy interaction where protective minor-safe sexual boundaries should have activated.
